instruction: Change the title on the first slide of this presentation to 'ChatGPT Prompt Engineering Guide' and save the file.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(1);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened terminal, installed python-pptx and python-docx, wrote a Python script to extract all slide text to a Word document. First attempt failed with XML compatibility error due to control characters in presentation. Second attempt with text cleaning also failed. Model got stuck in a response loop.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open terminal, run shell commands, install pip packages, write Python scripts, interact with LibreOffice Impress GUI
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed to create script.docx because python-docx threw ValueError on control characters (\x0b) in the presentation text. The regex cleaning pattern was incorrectly escaped in the heredoc. Model then got stuck in an infinite </think> loop.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified from full text extraction to a single slide title edit, which is achievable through Impress GUI or a simpler python-pptx script without the XML character issue
metadata.explanation: Task asks to change the title on slide 1. Evaluator uses a custom getter to read the PPTX file and extract the title text from slide 1, then a metric checks if it matches the expected value. Postconfig saves the file before evaluation.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements: title change (via getter + metric) and file save (via postconfig Ctrl+S before reading from disk)
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_title') without wrapping in rules
Expected value 'ChatGPT Prompt Engineering Guide' exactly matches the instruction requirement
Case-insensitive comparison in metric is reasonable for title text verification

Minor concern: Getter identifies 'title' by taking the first shape with a text_frame rather than using slide.shapes.title or checking placeholder type. This could misidentify a subtitle or other text box as the title in non-standard presentations, though it will likely work for most standard PPTX files
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using python-pptx's slide.shapes.title property or checking shape.placeholder_format.idx == 0 to more reliably identify the title placeholder, instead of assuming the first text-frame shape is the title
